catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is phonemic, but does not carry a high functional load and need not be written. A few pairs of words are contrastive by stress alone: o'to 'part' mi'miŋ 'earthquake' 'oto 'lightweight' 'mimiŋ 'to scratch' ... Conventions: Orthographic Phonemic stress is not written.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both parts of the deciding quotation are verbatim on physical p.4 of the OPD PDF we hold, exactly as the locator says. (2) The classification lexical rests on a primary SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (2000, rev. 1996) by the fieldworkers with ~19 years in the language, giving explicit stress-only minimal pairs (o'to/'oto, mi'miŋ/'mimiŋ); grade publisher-text is correct. It is short (5 pp.) but primary and the most recent statement by the only linguists who have described Anjam. (3) Glottolog's descriptive bibliography (3 items) contains no published grammar or phonology; the only fuller sources are unpublished 1983 SIL manuscripts by the same authors (phonemic statement; 110-pp grammar essentials), which could refine (add a default position or morphological behaviour) but are very unlikely to overturn phonemic stress asserted with minimal pairs in the authors' later OPD
